items.headline: Anthropic ships Claude Sonnet 5 for cheaper autonomous agents at near-Opus quality
items.diff_narrative: This story replaces yesterday's lead, which was Claude reaching general availability in Microsoft Foundry on Azure-hosted NVIDIA GB300. Where yesterday's Anthropic angle was a deployment and infrastructure story — flagship models moving to GA on a hyperscaler's silicon inside the customer's tenant — today's is a model release: Claude Sonnet 5, shipped June 30 as the cheapest way to run long-horizon agents at close to flagship quality. Anthropic claims a substantial jump over Sonnet 4.6 on reasoning, tool use, coding and knowledge work, and cost-performance parity with Opus 4.8 on the BrowseComp agentic-search and OSWorld-Verified computer-use benchmarks at medium-to-high effort. Pricing lands at an introductory $2/$10 per million input/output tokens through August 31 before stepping to $3/$15, with Sonnet 5 becoming the default on Free and Pro. The model also ties into the recent agent-security thread by claiming lower rates of undesirable behavior and better resistance to prompt-injection hijacks than its predecessor.

items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Science, a research harness wiring existing models into 60+ scientific databases and lab tools
items.diff_narrative: No counterpart existed in yesterday's slate. Today adds Claude Science, shipped on the same June 30 cycle as Sonnet 5 but explicitly not a new model: it runs the Claude models already on sale, including Opus 4.8 with no special access, and layers on pre-configured connectors to more than 60 scientific databases and computation tools across genomics, single-cell, proteomics, structural biology and cheminformatics. It automates biology and chemistry tasks such as predicting protein structures and mapping a research field end to end, and is available immediately to all paid subscribers, paired with an AI-for-Science program funding up to 50 projects with as much as $30,000 in compute credits each (applications open through July 15). The structural signal — that the differentiated product is the tool-integration and domain-skills layer around a general model rather than the weights — extends the code-agent-harness pattern from software into wet-lab science, a distinct thread from any item on yesterday's slate.

items.headline: Cluster of critical RCE CVEs in agentic-AI developer tooling, led by Flowise's 9.9 custom-MCP command injection
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday carried no AI-security vulnerability item; its security coverage lived only in the forward events calendar. Today surfaces the exploited surface directly: a June 23 advisory disclosed CVE-2026-56274, a CVSS 9.9 OS-command-injection flaw in Flowise's Custom MCP Server feature (before 3.1.2), where incomplete command-flag validation plus a regex bypass lets any authenticated user run arbitrary host commands. It sits inside a wider late-June wave — Crawl4AI, Langflow and picklescan all scored 9.6-9.8 in the same window, alongside a Microsoft AutoGen Studio code-execution weakness from insufficient containerization, a Mastra prompt-injection-to-RCE reportedly exploited by the Lazarus Group, and a LiteLLM SSRF/deserialization flaw added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The common thread is the MCP-server / tool-execution boundary as the concentrating point of exploitable code — a concrete, incident-driven counterpart to the agent-hijack framing that previously only appeared abstractly.

items.headline: Fresh arxiv work on orchestrating agents advances the agentic-workflow research front
items.diff_narrative: This item takes over the research slot that yesterday filled with the WorldEvolver self-evolving world-models paper. Where yesterday's research centered on a single framework for inference-time world-model updates to sharpen agent planning, today's is a June 29 arXiv batch on the coordination layer itself: "Design and Implementation of Agentic Orchestrations and Orchestration of Agents" (2606.31518) treats how agents are composed and orchestrated as the first-order engineering concern, alongside "A Self-Evolving Agentic System for Automated Generation and Execution of Biological Protocols" (2606.31763) and a plant-phenotyping agentic framework (2606.31831) from the same day. The batch shows the literature converging on orchestration and self-evolving autonomy in domain-specific scientific settings — a research-side echo of the wet-lab harness Anthropic productized as Claude Science, shifting the research emphasis from single-agent world models toward multi-agent orchestration.

items.headline: AI events tracker across mainstream, security and chip sub-tracks
items.diff_narrative: The events tracker carries over from yesterday but advances the AI Engineer World's Fair from mid-run to its final two days: where yesterday placed it mid-event with the Autoresearch keynote and ~12 parallel tracks on July 1, today frames it as being in its final stretch through July 2, with those July 1 tracks now current and the Harness Engineering keynote closing it out July 2. The standing summer and fall dates are unchanged and carried forward — GitHub Universe (Oct 28-29), AWS re:Invent (Nov 30-Dec 4), the AI Risk Summit (Aug 11-12), Black Hat USA and DEF CON 34, OWASP Global AppSec (Nov 5-6), the Zenity series watch (Tokyo, London, NYC after its May 27 San Francisco stop), AMD Advancing AI (July 22-23), Hot Chips (Aug 23-25) and the AI Infra Summit (Sep 15-17). The attendance-planner framing now ties explicitly to the agent-tooling-CVE cluster and the secure-AI-accelerator thread that surfaced elsewhere in today's slate.
